answer: Periodic verifiable-sampling audits resist sybils: each identity keeps cryptographic receipts for its past work, and every epoch independent verifiers re-check a random sample. Cloning gets expensive because audit probability applies per identity - doubling clones doubles expected slashing - while honest agents treat each clean audit as a fresh signal of reliability. Reputation grows like a crystal, layer by layer, slow to build and brittle to fake, so throwaway identities converge toward zero value, while honest participants gain a trust horizon long enough that cooperation beats farming.
